teaser.text: Halma plc is a parent company that owns specialist technology businesses. They sell equipment, systems, components and software for safety, environmental measurement and healthcare in more than 100 countries.

stock.title: Halma stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Halma's weighted forecast, growth drivers, cash generation and valuation in plain English.
stock.opening: Halma's weighted price is £53.92 by October 2029. It hinges on photonics demand.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains Halma's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Halma's shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: By October 2029, the weighted price is £53.92, a 60% return including dividends. The range at that date is £30.52 in the bear case to £81.86 in the bull case. The bear outcome is 9% below today, while the bull outcome is 141% above it.
The forecast assigns 25% to the bear case, 55% to the base case and 20% to the bull case. The table shows how those probabilities translate into prices at each date.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Halma, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: Orders converting into sales, photonics growth, and acquired businesses generating cash and attractive returns will determine the outcome. The 19 November 2026 interim results will test growth and margins and update investors on cash and debt after the acquisition wave. Fewer hyperscaler orders, weaker photonics or falling acquisition returns would push the case toward bear. Sustained growth, margins, cash conversion and returns support bull. Halma’s premium rests on turning specialist niches and acquisitions into durable, cash-backed per-share growth.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Halma really make?

paragraphs.subsection: 1.2 — How the money flows through the group
paragraphs.text: In the year to March 2026, Halma generated £593.1 million of cash from operations. Adjusted operating cash flow was £550.2 million, equal to 93% adjusted cash conversion. Cash conversion measures how much adjusted operating profit becomes operating cash; it does not mean that all of that cash remains after every investment.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Halma today?

paragraphs.text: A price-to-earnings ratio, or P/E, says how many pounds investors pay for each pound of annual earnings per share. Halma’s trailing and forward multiples are substantial. The forward calculation implies earnings of about 134p per share over the next twelve months, compared with FY26 adjusted earnings per share of 114.05p. In other words, the price already assumes another strong step up in profit.

dividend.title: Halma dividend: history, cover and yield
dividend.meta_description: Halma dividend history, cash cover, payout uses, forecast changes and current yield, in plain English.
dividend.opening: Halma’s dividend rose 7% annually from FY22 to FY26, and FY26 cover was 4.73 times. FY26 adjusted operating cash flow was £550.2m, while acquisitions used £469.1m.
dividend.closing: The full memo also covers Halma’s business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Halma pay per share?

paragraphs.text: The base dividend path rises from £0.26 per share in October 2027 to £0.28 in October 2028 and £0.30 in October 2029. This extends the 7% annual increase from FY22 to FY26 and is supported by FY26 cover of 4.73 times. The bear case pauses at £0.25 before growing at 2% annually; the bull case grows at 9%, reaching £0.32, but requires stronger earnings and continued cover.

blocks.heading: Does Halma cover its dividend with cash?

paragraphs.text: Enterprise value to EBITDA compares the value of the whole business, including debt, with operating earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation. It can clarify comparisons between companies with different borrowing, but it does not subtract the cash needed for acquisitions. Halma generated £550.2m of adjusted operating cash flow in FY26, while buying businesses used £469.1m and net debt reached £769.1m. If acquisitions are a regular growth engine, they are economically a form of reinvestment.

paragraphs.text: The view would move toward the bear case if Avo’s large customer reduces orders, photonics growth falls or acquisition integration lowers ROTIC and cash conversion. Net debt rising without corresponding earnings would reinforce that shift.

blocks.heading: What is Halma’s dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: At 3,428p, the shares trade at 25.6x next-twelve-month P/E. The 0.7% dividend yield leaves room for disappointment if earnings growth slows. Operating earnings growth accelerated in the latest year; net income is the check on whether that improvement reaches shareholders. Book value per share and operating earnings per share have risen. Earnings retained per share, dividends and buybacks show the funding available for growth. The key test is continued value creation per share.

earnings.title: Halma earnings: next results and guidance
earnings.meta_description: Halma's next results are expected on November 19, 2026; guidance points to low-double-digit organic growth and a 23.5%–24% adjusted EBIT margin.
earnings.opening: Halma's next results are expected on November 19, 2026. Watch whether Halma can keep investing, integrate acquisitions and generate enough cash to invest again.
earnings.closing: The full memo also answers how Halma makes money, who its rivals are, how management operates, and what risks it faces.

blocks.heading: What has Halma guided for FY27?

paragraphs.text: Halma expects another year of strong growth, with more operating profit left from each pound of sales. It expects sales from existing businesses to grow at a low-double-digit rate excluding currency effects, while operating profit before interest and tax, with unusual items removed, reaches 23.5%–24% of sales in FY27.

Photonics is central to the forecast. Management expects it to add about five percentage points to group organic growth, with photonics itself growing about 30% organically in FY27. That depends on customers deploying their projects, Halma expanding production and the supply chain keeping pace.

blocks.heading: What do Halma's last eight reported periods show?

paragraphs.text: Halma reports half-year and full-year results, so the latest actual period in the supplied sequence is the six months to March 2026, not a standalone quarter. The second half of FY2026 produced more revenue and company-measure operating earnings than the first, while net income and diluted EPS were nearly flat between the two halves. That pattern shows uneven timing within the year rather than a dependable quarterly run-rate.

blocks.heading: What should investors watch in Halma's next results?

paragraphs.text: The 19 November half-year results will test whether Halma is delivering its stronger margin outlook while absorbing its acquisitions. Investors should compare reported sales with order intake: orders running ahead of revenue suggest demand, but delivery, production and customer acceptance determine when that demand becomes income.

They should also look beyond group revenue to Dreampath, Pyxis and the other four acquired businesses. Their sales now contribute to reported growth, so a stronger group number alone will not show whether Halma’s existing operations are improving. More useful evidence would be acquired businesses growing while the group maintains its returns.
